Find modules jointly across species

Source: R/joint_modules.R
joint_modules.Rd

Clusters the networks of all species and their hogs as one graph. Labels are shared: the same label in two species is the same module. The hog table shows which hogs keep their copies in one module.

Usage

joint_modules(
  nets,
  orthologs,
  weight = NULL,
  objective = c("modularity", "CPM"),
  resolution = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  engine = "star"
)

Arguments

nets

Named list of at least two compute_network() results, dense or sparse. The names are the species.

orthologs

Long table with columns species, gene, hog, or a file for read_orthologs().

weight

Weight of the edge from a copy to its hog. NULL uses the median of all scaled co-expression edge weights.

objective

Leiden objective: "modularity" or "CPM".

resolution

Leiden resolution. NULL uses 1 for modularity. For CPM it uses the edge density of the joint graph.

seed

Integer seed, or NULL to use the current stream.

engine

Clustering engine. Only "star" exists.

Value

A list with:

modules

Named list with one module assignment per species, in the order of nets. Each has the as_modules() shape: modules (named integer vector, gene -> label), module_genes, n_modules, method = "joint" and params.

hogs

Data frame with one row per hog node, sorted by hog: hog, n_copies (genes linked), n_modules (distinct labels among the copies), module_main (the label with most copies; a tie goes to the smallest label) and copies_main (copies in it).

params

List of weight (the value used), objective, resolution, engine and seed.

modularity

Modularity of the joint graph, hog nodes included.

Details

The graph is a star expansion. Each species adds its genes and the edges at or above its threshold. Edge weights are divided by that species' largest weight, so every species lies on the same scale. No edge crosses species. Each hog with two or more copies among the genes adds one hog node. An edge of weight weight links the hog node to each copy. Hog nodes carry no other edge. Leiden clusters this graph; the modules then leave out the hog nodes. weight is the coupling between the co-expression edges and the hogs. A small weight gives per-species modules; a large one pulls the copies of a hog together. The default, the median co-expression weight, is a guess until a sweep over weight tests it. For CPM, .leiden_weights() scales every edge by the graph maximum, hog edges included; params$weight keeps the unscaled value.

See also

detect_modules() for one species, module_preservation() to test a module in another species.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- joint_modules(list(A = net_a, B = net_b), "orthologs.tsv",
  seed = 1
)
res$hogs[res$hogs$n_modules > 1, ]
pres <- module_preservation(res$modules$A, net_a, net_b, ortho)
} # }
